observations.finding: Compact recovery-and-extraction loop works and supports choosing archive order, optic kills, bypassing enemies and phase movement. Extraction concentrates meaningful pressure after fairly forgiving travel. Two successful attempts even with low accuracy and missed holds suggest generous objective/supply balance.

Rain, cyan strips, amber engineering lights, reflective floor and large Heart ring create a cohesive industrial mood. Menu and completion typography are strong. Enemy bodies, rifle, room props and distant silhouettes remain visibly simple/blocky, with repeated cover shapes and limited environmental variety.

Brief and handbook clearly explain map, core recovery, extraction and controls. Map provides useful room layout. Actual receiver reach was stricter than my visual impression of the floor ring, causing repeated too-far holds and premature departures. Prompt did say MOVE CLOSER, so this was readable feedback plus player error.

Objective beacons and extraction percentage are easy to find; visible optic/charge colors and phase break announcement communicate useful state. Small peripheral text, several simultaneous chevrons, world labels and lower readouts take attention from tiny distant enemies. Brief damage snapshots sometimes precede slightly later screenshots (e.g. 68 UI health versus 55 screenshot), consistent with live capture timing.

Natural route choices exposed entry, central yard, west triage/medical service, archives, east maintenance/engineering, Heart relay and extraction. Walls and low cover repeatedly blocked direct beacon travel; signage/map helped, but some obstacle correction happened only after seeing unchanged distance.

A coherent playable vertical slice with polished graphic direction, but observed geometry/animation detail, enemy variety, mission length and combat feedback do not yet establish full AAA production readiness. This rating concerns observed scope/finish, not project potential.
